title: Surgery for an undescended testicle in a boy
what: The surgeon brings your child's testicle down into the scrotum and fixes it there. The surgery is done under general anesthesia.
why: When one or both of a boy's testicles have not moved down into the scrotum on their own. It is usually done at an early age. The doctor will tell you when.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; you often go home the same day or the next day
tell_doctor: What illnesses your child has had and has now
All the medicines your child takes
If your child or anyone in the family had problems with anesthesia
A cold or fever before surgery. Be sure to tell the doctor

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Tests and a checkup with a pediatrician. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: The anesthesiologist will talk with you and ask about your child's health.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Children usually fast for a shorter time than adults. The clinic will tell you the exact times for food and drinks.

prepare.title: Talking to your child
prepare.text: Explain in simple words: they will sleep, and the doctor will fix it. Bring a favorite toy.

bring: A favorite toy, a change of clothes, and diapers if needed
steps: Usually you stay with your child until the operating room
The anesthesiologist gives anesthesia, often through a mask, and your child falls asleep
Through a small cut, the surgeon brings the testicle down into the scrotum
Your child wakes up and is brought back to you
feel: After anesthesia, your child may be sleepy or fussy
The groin may hurt. Your child will get children's pain medicine
Swelling and bruising of the scrotum can happen and go away
after: Active games, cycling, and similar activities are usually not allowed for a couple of weeks
Wound care and bathing as the doctor says
A follow-up visit when the surgeon schedules it
Later, the testicle is checked at regular checkups
red_flags: Your child is limp, refuses to drink, or keeps vomiting: call emergency services

faq.q: Can we wait in case it comes down on its own?
faq.a: If it has not come down in the first months, it usually will not. A pediatric surgeon will tell you the right time for surgery.

faq.q: Is anesthesia dangerous for a child?
faq.a: Anesthesia for children is well established. The anesthesiologist will explain everything and answer your questions.

reminders.text: Your child's surgery is tomorrow. Bring documents, a toy, and clothes. Food and drinks only until the time the clinic gave you.
